doc: Orthogonal regions. Transitions selected for the same event fire in one microstep: all exits, then all transition actions, then all entries.

steps.doc: Both regions move; their exit sets do not overlap.
A -e2-> Out leaves Q, which overlaps B -e2-> B2. Neither source contains the other, so the one selected first (A, earlier in document order) wins.
A -e3-> A2 is selected first; B -e3-> Out would exit A too, so it is dropped.
B -e4-> B2 is out of a substate of Q, so it beats Q -e4-> Out even though Q's was found first (from A).
